_comment: Two sections. `_ignore` is text the artboard shows as a SAMPLE — the running page renders it from seeded data or from what the visitor entered, so it is not copy the implementation is missing. Everything NOT listed there is structural copy and has to appear on the page. The rest of the keys are the BOX map: { appSelector: artboardSelector }. Only the pairing is declared here — every expected value is read off the artboard, so this file can never quietly assert the wrong number. `skip` drops one property from one box, and each use has to say why.

.cl-wiz__panel.why: min-width:0 is what lets a grid child shrink below its content. The artboard is a fixed 1440 frame that never has to, so it declares none; without it here the panel refuses to narrow and pushes the summary off-screen.

.cl-wiz__svc.why: Two of these three tracks are `auto`, so their pixel widths are the measured width of the text inside them - the artboard renders offline against a fallback face, the app against Nunito. That is a font-metric artifact, not a design value. The declared half of the design is asserted instead, on .cl-wiz__svc-add's minWidth and the row's gap, padding and alignment.

.cl-wiz__svc-add.why: The artboard fills a selected chip with Sky600 #0284C7. White 15px/700 on it measures 4.1 against a 4.5 floor, so .cl-chip--on shipped as Sky700 #0369A1 after the home-page contrast pass. The accessibility floor is newer than the artboard and wins; check-home-contrast.mjs enforces it.

.cl-wiz__advance.why: The artboard draws the shared .btn at its old 56px with 34px flanks. The owner ruled buttons to 40px after the home page shipped, and that ruling is newer than the artboard, so height and the padding that follows from it are deliberately not asserted here. Width, radius, colour, margin and alignment still are.
